reports.title: EDWARDS LIFESCIENCES REPORTS THIRD QUARTER RESULTS

guidance.heading: 2026 Outlook
section: •Increasing total company sales2 growth guidance to approximately 11.5% from 10% to 11%
•Increasing TAVR sales2 growth guidance to 9.0% to 9.5% from 8% to 9%
•Increasing TMTT sales guidance to $780 to $790 million from $760 to $780 million
•Increasing adjusted EPS guidance to $2.97 to $3.05 from $2.95 to $3.05, growing 18% at midpoint versus prior year
•2026 performance and milestone achievements reinforce long-term durable growth

desk.headline: Sales up 10.5% to $1.7bn, adjusted EPS $0.80 beat; 2026 sales, TAVR, TMTT and EPS outlook raised
results: Sales rose 10.5% to $1.7bn (11.2% in constant currency), with the US up 11% and outside the US up 11.5% in constant currency.
TAVR heart valves grew 8% to $1.24bn on stable prices; mitral and tricuspid devices (TMTT) jumped 44% to $207m.
Adjusted EPS rose 19% to $0.80; GAAP EPS was $0.53 after a $220m impairment of an acquired research asset.
Adjusted operating margin widened to 30.3% from 27.5% as R&D fell to 16.4% of sales.
About $700m of shares bought back so far this year, $1.3bn left on the authorisation; cash $3.1bn against about $0.6bn of debt.

guidance.summary: Edwards lifted its 2026 outlook for total, TAVR and TMTT sales and raised the bottom of its adjusted EPS range. It also set Q4 sales at $1.67–1.75bn and adjusted EPS at $0.61–0.69.

points: Management saw encouraging TAVR procedure growth leaving Q3 and expects future growth to come mainly from more procedures rather than share gains.
The PROGRESS trial in moderate aortic stenosis and Medicare's updated TAVR coverage were called a turning point, but their effect is expected to build gradually.
Edwards expects to lose a little share over time as competition grows, offset by market growth; share is now stable quarter to quarter.
Mitral and tricuspid procedures keep growing at double-digit rates, helped by new US approvals for the PASCAL system.
2027 guidance and more on timing for a moderate-AS indication are due at the December investor conference.
